title: Compute the first-shell trace for every physical shear covariance
statement: On the normalized unit 3-torus let kappa=2pi,E=span_R{sqrt(2)e_a cos(kappa x_b),sqrt(2)e_a sin(kappa x_b):a!=b},dim12. Let A_F=P_R P[(F.grad)(.)+((.).grad)F]P_R with orthogonal Fourier Galerkin P_R including E and all first shifted modes; |k|<=2 suffice. For EVERY F in E and ANY L2-orthonormal basis(u_j) of E, sum_j[<u_j,A_F^2u_j>+||A_Fu_j||2^2]=2kappa^2||F||2^2, independently of higher cutoff. For coordinate cos shear, explicit norm-minus-return-loop Fourier sums on positive axes are0,0,2, with negative modes equal. Translation/reflection and wavevector-loop closure kill every cross coefficient and cover all phases/combinations. In finite Stratonovich dV=-sum A_(F_alpha)V circle dB_alpha, arbitrary PSD covariance on E factors this way, so sum_j D(u_j)=2kappa^2 sum||F_alpha||2^2 and some initial basis input has D>=kappa^2 sum||F_alpha||2^2/6>0 for nonzero covariance. Drift nu Delta changes the trace to2kappa^2 sum||F_alpha||2^2-24nu kappa^2; strength>12nu forces some positive initial derivative. This is a finite-mode infinitesimal obstruction to universal mean-square nonexpansiveness for this fixed spatial/covariance family. It is not a finite-time, spectral-growth, WE or full common-force impossibility theorem.
